steps.title: Key Concept
steps.body: The UK's varied geology and climate have produced a diverse range of physical landscapes, including rugged upland areas, rolling lowlands, dramatic coastlines and extensive river valleys. The underlying geology is the fundamental control on landscape type.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Upland areas are generally above 200 metres in altitude, with rugged, steep terrain. They are found predominantly in the north and west of the UK on resistant igneous and metamorphic rocks.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Lowland areas are generally below 200 metres in altitude, with gentler, rolling terrain. They are found predominantly in the south and east of the UK on softer sedimentary rocks.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The UK's river systems are divided by major watersheds. The Pennines form the main watershed, with rivers flowing east to the North Sea or west to the Irish Sea. The River Severn and Thames drain the largest catchments in England and Wales.

steps.body: Describe the distribution of upland and lowland areas in the UK. (3 marks) | Explain how geology influences the UK's landscape. (4 marks) | Compare the characteristics of glaciated and non-glaciated landscapes in the UK. (6 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the specific names and locations of key upland and lowland areas Always link landscape features to their geological cause Use the north-west/upland vs south-east/lowland pattern as your organising principle Know at least 3 specific upland and 3 specific lowland areas with their geology For evaluation questions, discuss geology, climate, glaciation and human activity as interacting factors Use named examples of rivers and their key features
